description:
FILED s445 (Fable, round-5 batch legs). io/open.t companion leg moved 127/34 -> 118/3 C_ok/C_notok. Mechanism established by recovery-loading the SAME emission (byte-identical body vs ad6553d) on both runtimes in a correct shadow t/: BASE aborts 2 forms ("The variable STDOUT is unbound" + a delete-directory error); HEAD aborts a form once then EVERY later print dies "Couldn t write to #<fd-stream descriptor 1>: Broken pipe" -- fd 1 itself is gone. Before #513 the initial dup of STDOUT failed, so the test s close/restore sequence never ran; now the dup works, the test closes STDOUT, and the restore spelling open(STDOUT, ">&", $save) does not actually re-attach descriptor 1. TEN dup rows FIXED in the same file (46-51, 94, 95, 112, 114 left the fails set), so the fix nets positive on honest rows; the loss is the un-restored region. Fix belongs beside %p-open-impl/%p-resolve-fh (the s446i code): opening a BUILTIN handle name from a dup source must re-bind the fd/stream that name denotes, incl. descriptor 1/2 so later writes reach the terminal. Probe first: perl semantics of open(STDOUT,">&",$save) after close(STDOUT) -- fd number reuse, buffering. Snapshot row spliced this session with this task as cause. Related: #542 (buffer interleaving), #529/#452 family (the bare-STDOUT unbound form, PRE-EXISTING, aborts one form on BOTH trees).
--- DONE s448n (Opus round-6 agent N), commit b3d011a ---

THE FILED DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG, and the correction is the finding.  The
"Couldn't write to #<fd-stream descriptor 1>: Broken pipe" aborts are NOT a lost
STDOUT restore: they are a FORKED CHILD writing to a pipe nobody reads.  perl's
t/io/open.t line 385 does `open(my $f, '-|', $p)` with $p a TIED scalar declared
by a `my` that sits before an in-block `package main;`; PCL loses that lexical
(#593, filed), hands the open an EMPTY command, and PCL took an empty command
for perl's BARE fork-open -- so the child went on running the whole file beside
its parent, racing it on the recovery loader's shared file offset.  That is why
the file measured 118/3, 136/25 and 137/24 on the SAME tree.  `open(STDOUT,">&",
$save)` itself was already correct (%p-open-dup's std branch).

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY BROKEN, and is fixed:

1. An open onto a standard handle NAME must MOVE the descriptor.  PCL registered
   the new stream under the name only, so `open(STDOUT,'>',$f); print "x"` went
   to the TERMINAL while `print STDOUT "x"` went to the file, and an exec'd child
   never followed.  ONE place knows the rule now -- %p-std-slot / %p-rebind-std /
   %p-std-rebuild -- and %p-install-fh consults it, so every opener follows
   (plain, in-memory, fork-pipe, socket, accept, pipe).  %p-open-dup's std branch
   held the only copy of the rebuild and shares it now.

2. `close(STDOUT)` did not free descriptor 1: the handle is a SYNONYM stream and
   CL close on a synonym stream does not close its target (probed: a fresh open
   after the close gets fd 1 in perl, fd 6 in PCL).  This is what made
   `open(STDOUT,'|-',CMD); print ...; close(STDOUT)` HANG.
   %p-close-maybe-pipe closes %p-stream-target's stream now.

3. A THREE-argument open with an EMPTY command is perl's ERROR (undef, $! =
   Broken pipe), not the bare fork-open, which is the TWO-argument
   `open(F,"-|")`.  The argument count travels from the p-open macro into
   %p-open-impl; nothing else can tell them apart.

MEASURED: gate 178/6005 PASS.  Full perl-tests sweep TOTAL passing 18319 ->
18321 with the ONLY movement being the two scalar.t rows #543 accounts for.
t/io/open.t is DETERMINISTIC again and up: snapshot 118/3 -> 136/25 (both the
parallel and the serial re-run agree).  The extra 22 failing rows are rows the
file could not reach before; several are honest new failures on #592 (no
FD_CLOEXEC) and #594 (bareword dup source).

GUARD: Pl/t/std-handle-open-01.t, 5 rows, every expectation the live perl answer
(5.40.3): the redirect reaching the default print AND a child; close(STDOUT)
freeing fd 1; STDOUT onto a pipe (the row that hung); the 3-arg empty command;
STDERR.  not-supported.md gains the in-memory std-handle entry (perl REFUSES
`open(STDOUT,'>',\$buf)` with EBADF; PCL allows it and leaves the descriptor
alone).

FOR THE MERGE REVIEW: baselines/perl-suite-run.tsv's io/open.t row moves
118/3 -> 136/25 (aborted-forms and the unreadable-form note go with it -- the
loader is no longer racing itself).  perl-tests baselines: see #543.

RESIDUE FILED: #592 (no FD_CLOEXEC anywhere, `fcntl` absent), #593 (the lost
in-block lexical -- the root cause above), #594 (a BAREWORD in the dup SOURCE
slot emits an unbound CL symbol).
title: Restoring STDOUT from a saved dup leaves fd 1 BROKEN -- open(STDOUT, ">&", $saved) does not reconnect descriptor 1, every later print aborts its form (exposed by #513; io/open.t C_ok 127->118)
